metadata.title: Bridging the Pixel Gap in Browser Automation.
metadata.purpose: Redo of an unbuilt Teardown scaffold as an hai-simple Plain-register question: why doesn't Claude's reported click coordinate land on the button on your real screen? Lands the carry-out that the coordinate is measured on a resized picture, not wrong.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B04 (same rectangle pair, same button)
metadata.one_flag: none — fully sourced from coordinate_scaling.py, see SOURCES.md

beats.narration_text: Claude reports a click at 728, 364. You'd assume that's your screen's exact spot. It isn't — it's scaled. Why does a coordinate need scaling before it becomes a real click?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude clicks at (728, 364) on my screens exact spot right?', hesitates on 'exact', corrects to 'scaled', lands the real question

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('exact' -> 'scaled') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Here's why. Claude never sees your actual screen. It sees a resized copy — 16:9 screenshots get squeezed to exactly 1456 by 819 pixels before the model looks at them. Your real viewport, 1920 by 1080, is a different size entirely. Same button, two different coordinate spaces.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — two rectangles, 1456x819 and 1920x1080, same button dot at different relative positions, bridged by a question mark

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — two spaces, one button
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Left rectangle labelled '1456 × 819 — what Claude sees' with a terracotta button dot. Right rectangle labelled '1920 × 1080 — your real screen', larger, same aspect. A question-mark arrow bridges them. THIS EXACT PAIR OF RECTANGLES RETURNS AT B04.

beats.narration_text: The obvious guess: click at 728, 364 and be done — Claude found the button. Try that on the real screen and you miss. The button never sat at 728, 364 in your 1920 by 1080 window; that was only its position in the smaller picture Claude saw.

shot.new_visual_element: Same anchor pair; raw (728,364) carried straight across onto the 1920x1080 rectangle — misses the button, struck

production_viz.label: Same raw pixel, wrong canvas
production_viz.mechanic: The B01 rectangle pair returns. The (728, 364) dot is carried across unscaled onto the 1920×1080 rectangle; it lands short of a target ring near center, marked with a cross. Caption: 'nowhere close to the button'.

beats.narration_text: The fix is the inverse of the resize ratio. Multiply by how much bigger your screen is: 1920 over 1456 for x, 1080 over 819 for y — both come out to about 1.32. Multiply Claude's coordinate by that, clamp it inside your screen's bounds, and you have the real click.

shot.new_visual_element: Formula card: real_x = x * (viewport_w / 1456), real_y = y * (viewport_h / 819), then a clamp note; source credit

production_viz.label: The inverse ratio
production_viz.mechanic: Two formula lines build in ink mono on cream: 'real_x = x × (viewport_w / 1456)' then 'real_y = y × (viewport_h / 819)'. Beneath, a smaller terracotta line: 'clamp to [0, viewport_w-1] / [0, viewport_h-1]'. Caption bottom-right: 'Source: Claude Quickstarts (Anthropic)'.

beats.narration_text: Apply that to Claude's number: 728 times 1920 over 1456 is 960. 364 by the same ratio is 480. Click there, and it lands exactly on the button. That math holds for the 16:9 screenshot Claude actually returns. Change the aspect ratio, and Claude resizes to a different fixed size — the ratio changes, but the same multiply-back idea still applies.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same rectangle pair, dot now scaled and lands on target; a third non-16:9 rectangle beside it, struck, captioned 'different lookup table'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — scaled, and it lands
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01/B02 RECTANGLE PAIR RETURNS, identical. This time (728, 364) is carried across with the ratio applied, landing exactly on the target ring at '(960, 480)' inside the 1920×1080 rectangle, marked with a check. Off to the side, a third, differently-proportioned rectangle appears, struck through, captioned 'not 16:9 — different table' — the caveat, not the main case.

beats.narration_text: A Claude coordinate isn't wrong — it's just measured on a smaller picture. Multiply back by the resize ratio, and the click lands exactly where you meant.

props.sparkLine: Resized picture, not a wrong number.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. My model clicks at seven hundred, four ten on a 1456 by 819 screenshot, but my screen is 1920 by 1080 — write the scaling and land the click exactly. Liam, in for Bear.
